names.name: Fried rice and chow mein
names.said: Kept in a warmer, sold by the scoop, priced under the sandwich.

text.what: Cooked rice stir-fried with egg, vegetables and meat, held hot in a steam table beside the donut case — with chow mein next to it in many shops.
text.story:
Fried rice is a staple of Chinese cooking and of American Chinese menus. In California donut shops it arrives for the same reason egg rolls do: the shop needs a second product at a second hour, and the kitchen can already do it.

Dorothy Chow's family business, B & H Bakery Distributors, supplies these shops; her father, a survivor of the Cambodian genocide, built it, she told KQED, "to help our own people."
text.today: A donut shop with a steam table is doing lunch, which is a different business from the one it does at five in the morning.
